flow.title: Solar Generation and Battery Storage: A Teacher's Guide
flow.summary: A concise 10-minute presentation to help teachers explain how solar panels convert sunlight into electricity and how batteries store that energy for later use, clarifying the interrelationship between generation and storage.

beats.title: Solar Panels: Turning Sunlight into Electricity
beats.speakerNotes: Introduce the core concept: solar panels act like converters, turning sunlight into electricity. Visualize this as a sun shining onto dark panels to spark energy.
beats.visualDirection: Show sunlight rays converging on a set of solar panels with small animated sparks of electricity appearing at the array

beats.title: Batteries: Storing Energy for Later
beats.speakerNotes: Explain that this electricity is only available when the sun shines. Batteries serve as the 'battery' that stores excess energy generated during the day for use at night or during cloudy weather.
beats.visualDirection: An animation where a battery fills up with energy bubbles during the day (sunny icon) and then is used to power lights//devices at night

beats.title: The Power of Partnership
beats.speakerNotes: Conclude by emphasizing the partnership: solar generation without storage is limited to daylight hours, while storage without generation offers no power source. Together, they create a sustainable energy loop.
beats.visualDirection: A simple two-step loop graphic showing Sun > Solar Panels > Electricity > Battery > Devices at night

**Proposal Summary:**

This three-beat flow simplifies the core relationship between generation and storage for a teacher audience:
1.  **Beat 1:** Defines solar panels as conversion devices (Sun \u2192 Electricity).
2.  **Beat 2:** Defines batteries as storage mechanisms (Daytime excess energy saved for night use).
3.  **Beat 3:** Synthesizes the dependency, illustrating how both functions are required for a complete system.

The flow uses the single available artifact (`solar-notes.md`) to guide the explanation, adding visual directions to clarify concepts since textual descriptions alone may lack impact.
